From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Kim — initial sketch attached. High level notes inside the sheet:

- Base assumptions: avg 50k tokens/day (spread evenly -> negligible baseline);
  surge = 2.5M tokens across 10 minutes -> ~4,166 tokens/sec sustained for 10m.
- Model choices: native FP16 70B -> ~12 tokens/sec per GPU (A100/RTX-class compute),
  30B quantized int8 -> ~35 tokens/sec per GPU (depends on kernel and batch).
- Conservative headroom (+3x): to sustain 4.2k tps peak we'd recommend a dedicated
  pool of 120 x 30B-quantized GPUs (assumes autoscaling + continuous batching).
- Aggressive (optimistic kernels + KV cache + prefix caching): 40 x 30B-quantized GPUs
  with warm caches, but tail-latency risk if cold starts occur.

Risks and mitigation:
- Tail (p99) latency can blow out if many long conversations hit cache miss simultaneously —
  recommend a warmup / prefill policy for expected high-traffic windows and a canary fallback
  model (quantized 13B) for graceful degradation to keep p95 within SLO.
- Recommend a burst buffer in Dedicated (reserve 20% extra pool) to absorb sudden spikes.

See attached: orbital_compute_estimate.xlsx (tabs: assumptions, conservative, aggressive, 
fallback_plan). I also added a quick SLO fit table that maps tokens/sec to expected p50/p95
latency by model variant.

Ben
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. To answer Kimberly's clarifying Qs:

- Traffic shape: 85% of volume concentrated between 9am-5pm PT with a visible

- Surge clarification: 2.5M tokens is the total span over the 10-minute window,

One ask: can you produce a short table that shows cost per token in the conservative

Elena

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sizing conversation follow-up (Orbital commit)

Following up on Ben's sheet — engineering notes for latency tail and ops: 

- If Orbital will pin the model version and allow our KV prefill for top 10% prefixes,
  we can reduce effective tokens/sec by up to 22% for conversational flows (measured
  on comparable customers). That materially reduces GPUs required in the aggressive plan.
- For p95=400ms target: quantized 30B with batching tuned and 2ms kernel latency depends
  on request size distribution. We should simulate with Orbital's real prompt mix —
  can you share a 24-hour sample trace?
- Suggest a staged rollout: start with 40 GPUs (aggressive config), run a traffic
  soak with real traces for 72h, measure p95/p99, then expand to conservative pool if
  we see persistent tail issues. This gives procurement a lower starting commit and
  ops time to validate the tail behavior.

I'll mock up the cost-per-token table (w/ KV on/off) and drop into the Drive link.

-Priyom
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
